title: They Don't Know What They Are Talking About When They Talk About Religion
coreMove: Interpret a belief system through what practitioners do, risk, and repeat, not only through literal statements.
sourcePressure: Detached outsiders misread religion when they treat it as propositions rather than embedded practice, ritual, and function.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the chapter into theology, culture-war commentary, or outsider sneering.

sourceAnchors.name: embedded religious practice
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar supports function, ritual, and lived use over detached literalism, with no named religious anecdote frozen.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The lived practice matters because a rule can mean one thing on paper and another thing when a community carries it with cost.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital chaplain explaining fasting rules to a medical team
exampleSpecs.audience: clinician learning practice cannot be read only as a proposition
exampleSpecs.stakes: patient trust depends on understanding function inside practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie Hart asks what the practice does for the patient before reducing it to a nutrition rule.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a meal tray cooling by a privacy curtain

exampleSpecs.domain: museum educator interpreting a ritual object without practitioners present
exampleSpecs.audience: educator seeing outsider description miss lived use
exampleSpecs.stakes: visitors may learn the object as dead text rather than practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Antoine invites a practitioner to describe when the object is handled, not just what it symbolizes.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cotton gloves hovering over a carved object

exampleSpecs.domain: manager scheduling around a religious holiday she does not understand
exampleSpecs.audience: team lead treating practice as lived constraint rather than preference trivia
exampleSpecs.stakes: staff dignity and project timing both depend on embedded knowledge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida Holm moves the deadline after asking which work would violate the practice, not which belief sounds important.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: calendar squares marked in two colors

exampleSpecs.domain: journalist writing about a congregation from one literal quotation
exampleSpecs.audience: reporter learning use and ritual change the meaning of words
exampleSpecs.stakes: readers may receive a false map from accurate quotation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James Bell sits through the service sequence before deciding what the quoted phrase means.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: folding chairs aligned before a small lectern

exampleSpecs.domain: teacher explaining dietary rules as mere superstition
exampleSpecs.audience: teacher correcting a detached lesson plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: students need function, identity, and practice without caricature
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya Shah rewrites the lesson after a student explains when the rule matters at home.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: lunch containers arranged by a classroom sink

exampleSpecs.domain: product team designing a prayer-space feature from survey text only
exampleSpecs.audience: designer needing embedded observation before building
exampleSpecs.stakes: a feature can insult users while satisfying literal requirements
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco Ruiz watches how people enter, pause, and leave before naming the feature complete.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: soft footsteps at the edge of a quiet room
